findings.summary: The resolution adds code that neither parent has. The legacy cleanup now also removes <uid>.lock, <uid>.new.* and <uid>.old.* under the old $TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg parent (lines 136-149). It does this without holding a lock. It also calls rmdir on the parent even when there is no legacy seed, which reviewed head 2892d609 only did together with removing the seed. The change is disclosed, tested, and consistent with what #1141 intends, so it is integration glue and not a lost behaviour.
findings.failure_scenario: Only possible while upgrading. Suppose a #1139-era installed helper is part-way through a rebuild under $TMPDIR/dsh-gnupg/<uid>.lock when the first call of the newly installed helper runs. The new call deletes that lock and the staging copy, so the old call's mv fails and that one signing exits 2. Every later call works. Reviewed head 2892d609 already had the same window for removing <uid> itself, so the size of the exposure is unchanged.
